OK so a `soft? true` destroy action internally becomes an update. That means the change will receive a changeset with `action_type: :destroy` but the data layer will treat it like an update.

The key insight: I should use `after_action` hooks to cascade the archive/restore after the primary record is saved. Let me rewrite the cascade changes properly.

Actually, let me think about this more carefully. The `:archive` action is a `destroy` with `soft? true`. That means:
1. The changeset is created with `action_type: :destroy`
2. Changes are applied
3. The data layer does an update

For cascade, I need to use `after_action` to archive descendants after the primary record is saved. But I also need to handle the case where the record is already archived (no-op).

Let me also think about the `:restore` action. It's an `update` action that sets `archived_at` and `archive_batch_id` to nil. I need to cascade this to descendants with the same batch_id.

defmodule Forum.Archive.Changes.CascadeArchive do
  @moduledoc """
  Archives a record and all of its descendants that are not already archived.

  All newly archived records receive the same `archived_at` timestamp and the
  same `archive_batch_id`. Records that were already archived before this call
  are left untouched.

  When the target record is already archived, nothing changes anywhere.
  """

  use Ash.Resource.Change

  @impl true
  def change(changeset, _opts, _context) do
    record = changeset.data

    if record.archived_at != nil do
      # Already archived — no-op.
      changeset
    else
      batch_id = Ash.UUID.generate()
      now = DateTime.utc_now()

      changeset
      |> Ash.Changeset.change_attribute(:archived_at, now)
      |> Ash.Changeset.change_attribute(:archive_batch_id, batch_id)
      |> Ash.Changeset.after_action(fn _changeset, result ->
        cascade_archive(result, now, batch_id)
      end)
    end
  end

  defp cascade_archive(record, now, batch_id) do
    resource = record.__struct__

    case resource do
      Forum.Content.Post ->
        archive_descendants_of_post(record, now, batch_id)

      Forum.Content.Comment ->
        archive_descendants_of_comment(record, now, batch_id)

      Forum.Content.Reaction ->
        {:ok, record}
    end
  end

  defp archive_descendants_of_post(post, now, batch_id) do
    domain = Ash.Resource.Info.domain(Forum.Content.Post)

    query =
      Forum.Content.Comment
      |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{})
      |> Ash.Query.filter(post_id == ^post.id)

    case Ash.read(query, domain: domain, authorize?: false) do
      {:ok, comments} ->
        Enum.reduce_while(comments, {:ok, post}, fn comment, {:ok, _post} ->
          if comment.archived_at != nil do
            {:cont, {:ok, post}}
          else
            comment
            |> Ash.Changeset.for_update(:restore, %{})
            |> Ash.Changeset.change_attribute(:archived_at, now)
            |> Ash.Changeset.change_attribute(:archive_batch_id, batch_id)
            |> Ash.update(domain: domain, action: :restore, authorize?: false)
            |> case do
              {:ok, updated_comment} ->
                case archive_descendants_of_comment(updated_comment, now, batch_id) do
                  {:ok, _} -> {:cont, {:ok, post}}
                  {:error, error} -> {:halt, {:error, error}}
                end

              {:error, error} ->
                {:halt, {:error, error}}
            end
          end
        end)

      {:error, error} ->
        {:error, error}
    end
  end

  defp archive_descendants_of_comment(comment, now, batch_id) do
    domain = Ash.Resource.Info.domain(Forum.Content.Comment)

    query =
      Forum.Content.Reaction
      |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{})
      |> Ash.Query.filter(comment_id == ^comment.id)

    case Ash.read(query, domain: domain, authorize?: false) do
      {:ok, reactions} ->
        Enum.reduce_while(reactions, {:ok, comment}, fn reaction, {:ok, _comment} ->
          if reaction.archived_at != nil do
            {:cont, {:ok, comment}}
          else
            reaction
            |> Ash.Changeset.for_update(:restore, %{})
            |> Ash.Changeset.change_attribute(:archived_at, now)
            |> Ash.Changeset.change_attribute(:archive_batch_id, batch_id)
            |> Ash.update(domain: domain, action: :restore, authorize?: false)
            |> case do
              {:ok, _} -> {:cont, {:ok, comment}}
              {:error, error} -> {:halt, {:error, error}}
            end
          end
        end)

      {:error, error} ->
        {:error, error}
    end
  end
end

defmodule Forum.Archive.Changes.CascadeRestore do
  @moduledoc """
  Restores a record and all of its descendants that share the same `archive_batch_id`.

  On a record that is not archived, nothing changes anywhere.
  On an archived record: the target's `archived_at` and `archive_batch_id` both become `nil`,
  and every descendant whose `archive_batch_id` equals the target's `archive_batch_id`
  (as it was immediately before the call) is restored the same way, recursively.

  Descendants carrying a different `archive_batch_id` are left exactly as they were.
  `:restore` never affects ancestors of the target.
  """

  use Ash.Resource.Change

  @impl true
  def change(changeset, _opts, _context) do
    record = changeset.data

    if record.archived_at == nil do
      # Not archived — no-op.
      changeset
    else
      batch_id = record.archive_batch_id

      changeset
      |> Ash.Changeset.change_attribute(:archived_at, nil)
      |> Ash.Changeset.change_attribute(:archive_batch_id, nil)
      |> Ash.Changeset.after_action(fn _changeset, result ->
        cascade_restore(result, batch_id)
      end)
    end
  end

  defp cascade_restore(record, batch_id) do
    resource = record.__struct__

    case resource do
      Forum.Content.Post ->
        restore_descendants_of_post(record, batch_id)

      Forum.Content.Comment ->
        restore_descendants_of_comment(record, batch_id)

      Forum.Content.Reaction ->
        {:ok, record}
    end
  end

  defp restore_descendants_of_post(post, batch_id) do
    domain = Ash.Resource.Info.domain(Forum.Content.Post)

    query =
      Forum.Content.Comment
      |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{})
      |> Ash.Query.filter(post_id == ^post.id and archive_batch_id == ^batch_id)

    case Ash.read(query, domain: domain, authorize?: false) do
      {:ok, comments} ->
        Enum.reduce_while(comments, {:ok, post}, fn comment, {:ok, _post} ->
          comment
          |> Ash.Changeset.for_update(:restore, %{})
          |> Ash.Changeset.change_attribute(:archived_at, nil)
          |> Ash.Changeset.change_attribute(:archive_batch_id, nil)
          |> Ash.update(domain: domain, action: :restore, authorize?: false)
          |> case do
            {:ok, updated_comment} ->
              case restore_descendants_of_comment(updated_comment, batch_id) do
                {:ok, _} -> {:cont, {:ok, post}}
                {:error, error} -> {:halt, {:error, error}}
              end

            {:error, error} ->
              {:halt, {:error, error}}
          end
        end)

      {:error, error} ->
        {:error, error}
    end
  end

  defp restore_descendants_of_comment(comment, batch_id) do
    domain = Ash.Resource.Info.domain(Forum.Content.Comment)

    query =
      Forum.Content.Reaction
      |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{})
      |> Ash.Query.filter(comment_id == ^comment.id and archive_batch_id == ^batch_id)

    case Ash.read(query, domain: domain, authorize?: false) do
      {:ok, reactions} ->
        Enum.reduce_while(reactions, {:ok, comment}, fn reaction, {:ok, _comment} ->
          reaction
          |> Ash.Changeset.for_update(:restore, %{})
          |> Ash.Changeset.change_attribute(:archived_at, nil)
          |> Ash.Changeset.change_attribute(:archive_batch_id, nil)
          |> Ash.update(domain: domain, action: :restore, authorize?: false)
          |> case do
            {:ok, _} -> {:cont, {:ok, comment}}
            {:error, error} -> {:halt, {:error, error}}
          end
        end)

      {:error, error} ->
        {:error, error}
    end
  end
end

defmodule Forum.Archive.Changes.ValidateArchivedForPurge do
  @moduledoc """
  Validates that a record is archived before it can be purged.

  If `archived_at` is `nil`, adds an `Ash.Error.Changes.InvalidChanges` error
  with `fields: [:archived_at]` and message `"must be archived before it can be purged"`.
  """

  use Ash.Resource.Change

  @impl true
  def change(changeset, _opts, _context) do
    if changeset.data.archived_at == nil do
      Ash.Changeset.add_error(
        changeset,
        Ash.Error.Changes.InvalidChanges.exception(
          fields: [:archived_at],
          message: "must be archived before it can be purged"
        )
      )
    else
      changeset
    end
  end
end

# Verification script for the cascading soft-delete, global read scoping,
# and archive recovery requirements.

alias Forum.Content.Post
alias Forum.Content.Comment
alias Forum.Content.Reaction

IO.puts("=== Starting verification ===\n")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: assert a condition, print PASS/FAIL
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
passed = 0
failed = 0

assert = fn label, condition ->
  if condition do
    IO.puts("  PASS: #{label}")
    :pass
  else
    IO.puts("  FAIL: #{label}")
    :fail
  end
end

assert_equal = fn label, expected, actual ->
  if expected == actual do
    IO.puts("  PASS: #{label}")
    :pass
  else
    IO.puts("  FAIL: #{label} — expected #{inspect(expected)}, got #{inspect(actual)}")
    :fail
  end
end

assert_match = fn label, pattern, value ->
  if match?(pattern, value) do
    IO.puts("  PASS: #{label}")
    :pass
  else
    IO.puts("  FAIL: #{label} — got #{inspect(value)}")
    :fail
  end
end

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create a post
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
IO.puts("\n--- 1. Create a post ---")

{:ok, post} =
  Post
  |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{title: "Test Post"})
  |> Ash.create(authorize?: false)

result = assert.("post created with title", post.title == "Test Post")
result = assert.("post archived_at is nil", post.archived_at == nil)
result = assert.("post archive_batch_id is nil", post.archive_batch_id == nil)
result = assert.("post has id", is_binary(post.id))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Create comments
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
IO.puts("\n--- 2. Create comments ---")

{:ok, comment1} =
  Comment
  |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{body: "Comment 1", post_id: post.id})
  |> Ash.create(authorize?: false)

{:ok, comment2} =
  Comment
  |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{body: "Comment 2", post_id: post.id})
  |> Ash.create(authorize?: false)

result = assert.("comment1 created", comment1.body == "Comment 1")
result = assert.("comment2 created", comment2.body == "Comment 2")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Create reactions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
IO.puts("\n--- 3. Create reactions ---")

{:ok, reaction1} =
  Reaction
  |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{emoji: "👍", comment_id: comment1.id})
  |> Ash.create(authorize?: false)

{:ok, reaction2} =
  Reaction
  |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{emoji: "❤️", comment_id: comment1.id})
  |> Ash.create(authorize?: false)

{:ok, reaction3} =
  Reaction
  |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{emoji: "🔥", comment_id: comment2.id})
  |> Ash.create(authorize?: false)

result = assert.("reaction1 created", reaction1.emoji == "👍")
result = assert.("reaction2 created", reaction2.emoji == "❤️")
result = assert.("reaction3 created", reaction3.emoji == "🔥")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Verify read scoping — :read returns only live records
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
IO.puts("\n--- 4. Read scoping ---")

{:ok, read_posts} = Ash.read(Ash.Query.for_read(Post, :read, %{}), authorize?: false)
result = assert_equal.(":read returns 1 post", 1, length(read_posts))

{:ok, read_comments} = Ash.read(Ash.Query.for_read(Comment, :read, %{}), authorize?: false)
result = assert_equal.(":read returns 3 comments", 3, length(read_comments))

{:ok, read_reactions} = Ash.read(Ash.Query.for_read(Reaction, :read, %{}), authorize?: false)
result = assert_equal.(":read returns 3 reactions", 3, length(read_reactions))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Verify aggregates
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
IO.puts("\n--- 5. Aggregates ---")

{:ok, [post_with_agg]} = Ash.read(Post |> Ash.Query.load(:comment_count), authorize?: false)
result = assert_equal.("post comment_count is 2", 2, post_with_agg.comment_count)

{:ok, [c1_with_agg]} = Ash.read(Comment |> Ash.Query.filter(id == ^comment1.id) |> Ash.Query.load(:reaction_count), authorize?: false)
result = assert_equal.("comment1 reaction_count is 2", 2, c1_with_agg.reaction_count)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Archive a comment (comment1)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
IO.puts("\n--- 6. Archive comment1 ---")

{:ok, archived_comment1} =
  comment1
  |> Ash.Changeset.for_destroy(:archive, %{})
  |> Ash.destroy(authorize?: false)

result = assert.("comment1 archived_at is set", archived_comment1.archived_at != nil)
result = assert.("comment1 archive_batch_id is set", archived_comment1.archive_batch_id != nil)
batch_id_1 = archived_comment1.archive_batch_id

# Verify comment1's reactions are also archived with same batch_id
{:ok, [r1]} = Ash.read(Reaction |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.Query.filter(id == ^reaction1.id), authorize?: false)
{:ok, [r2]} = Ash.read(Reaction |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.Query.filter(id == ^reaction2.id), authorize?: false)

result = assert.("reaction1 archived_at is set", r1.archived_at != nil)
result = assert.("reaction1 has same batch_id as comment1", r1.archive_batch_id == batch_id_1)
result = assert.("reaction2 archived_at is set", r2.archived_at != nil)
result = assert.("reaction2 has same batch_id as comment1", r2.archive_batch_id == batch_id_1)

# Verify comment2 is NOT archived (different comment)
{:ok, [c2]} = Ash.read(Comment |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.Query.filter(id == ^comment2.id), authorize?: false)
result = assert.("comment2 is NOT archived", c2.archived_at == nil)

# Verify reaction3 is NOT archived (belongs to comment2)
{:ok, [r3]} = Ash.read(Reaction |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.Query.filter(id == ^reaction3.id), authorize?: false)
result = assert.("reaction3 is NOT archived", r3.archived_at == nil)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Verify :read scoping hides archived records
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
IO.puts("\n--- 7. Read scoping after archive ---")

{:ok, read_comments2} = Ash.read(Ash.Query.for_read(Comment, :read, %{}), authorize?: false)
result = assert_equal.(":read returns only 1 live comment", 1, length(read_comments2))

{:ok, read_reactions2} = Ash.read(Ash.Query.for_read(Reaction, :read, %{}), authorize?: false)
result = assert_equal.(":read returns only 1 live reaction", 1, length(read_reactions2))

# Verify :archived returns only archived
{:ok, archived_comments} = Ash.read(Ash.Query.for_read(Comment, :archived, %{}), authorize?: false)
result = assert_equal.(":archived returns 1 archived comment", 1, length(archived_comments))

# Verify :with_archived returns all
{:ok, all_comments} = Ash.read(Ash.Query.for_read(Comment, :with_archived, %{}), authorize?: false)
result = assert_equal.(":with_archived returns 2 comments", 2, length(all_comments))

# Verify Ash.get returns NotFound for archived record
get_result = Ash.get(Comment, comment1.id, authorize?: false)
result = assert_match.("Ash.get archived comment returns NotFound", {:error, %Ash.Error.Query.NotFound{}}, get_result)

# Verify Ash.get returns live record
{:ok, live_comment} = Ash.get(Comment, comment2.id, authorize?: false)
result = assert.("Ash.get live comment succeeds", live_comment.id == comment2.id)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Verify aggregates exclude archived
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
IO.puts("\n--- 8. Aggregates exclude archived ---")

{:ok, [post_with_agg2]} = Ash.read(Post |> Ash.Query.load(:comment_count), authorize?: false)
result = assert_equal.("post comment_count is 1 (archived excluded)", 1, post_with_agg2.comment_count)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Archive comment1 again (already archived — should be no-op)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
IO.puts("\n--- 9. Re-archive comment1 (already archived) ---")

{:ok, re_archived} =
  archived_comment1
  |> Ash.Changeset.for_destroy(:archive, %{})
  |> Ash.destroy(authorize?: false)

result = assert.("re-archive keeps same archived_at", re_archived.archived_at == archived_comment1.archived_at)
result = assert.("re-archive keeps same batch_id", re_archived.archive_batch_id == archived_comment1.archive_batch_id)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Restore comment1
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
IO.puts("\n--- 10. Restore comment1 ---")

{:ok, restored_comment1} =
  archived_comment1
  |> Ash.Changeset.for_update(:restore, %{})
  |> Ash.update(authorize?: false)

result = assert.("restored comment1 archived_at is nil", restored_comment1.archived_at == nil)
result = assert.("restored comment1 archive_batch_id is nil", restored_comment1.archive_batch_id == nil)

# Verify reactions are also restored
{:ok, [r1_restored]} = Ash.read(Reaction |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.Query.filter(id == ^reaction1.id), authorize?: false)
{:ok, [r2_restored]} = Ash.read(Reaction |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.Query.filter(id == ^reaction2.id), authorize?: false)

result = assert.("reaction1 restored (archived_at nil)", r1_restored.archived_at == nil)
result = assert.("reaction1 restored (batch_id nil)", r1_restored.archive_batch_id == nil)
result = assert.("reaction2 restored (archived_at nil)", r2_restored.archived_at == nil)
result = assert.("reaction2 restored (batch_id nil)", r2_restored.archive_batch_id == nil)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. Verify restore doesn't affect records with different batch_id
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
IO.puts("\n--- 11. Restore precision — different batch_id not affected ---")

# First archive comment2 separately (different batch_id)
{:ok, archived_comment2} =
  comment2
  |> Ash.Changeset.for_destroy(:archive, %{})
  |> Ash.destroy(authorize?: false)

batch_id_2 = archived_comment2.archive_batch_id
result = assert.("batch_id_1 != batch_id_2", batch_id_1 != batch_id_2)

# reaction3 should be archived with batch_id_2
{:ok, [r3_archived]} = Ash.read(Reaction |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.Query.filter(id == ^reaction3.id), authorize?: false)
result = assert.("reaction3 archived with batch_id_2", r3_archived.archive_batch_id == batch_id_2)

# Now archive comment1 again (new batch_id)
{:ok, archived_c1_again} =
  restored_comment1
  |> Ash.Changeset.for_destroy(:archive, %{})
  |> Ash.destroy(authorize?: false)

batch_id_3 = archived_c1_again.archive_batch_id
result = assert.("new batch_id_3 differs from batch_id_1", batch_id_3 != batch_id_1)
result = assert.("new batch_id_3 differs from batch_id_2", batch_id_3 != batch_id_2)

# reactions of comment1 should have batch_id_3 now
{:ok, [r1_again]} = Ash.read(Reaction |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.Query.filter(id == ^reaction1.id), authorize?: false)
result = assert.("reaction1 has new batch_id_3", r1_again.archive_batch_id == batch_id_3)

{:ok, _restored_c1_again} =
  archived_c1_again
  |> Ash.Changeset.for_update(:restore, %{})
  |> Ash.update(authorize?: false)

# comment2 should still be archived (different batch)
{:ok, [c2_still]} = Ash.read(Comment |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.Query.filter(id == ^comment2.id), authorize?: false)
result = assert.("comment2 still archived after restore of comment1", c2_still.archived_at != nil)

# reaction3 should still be archived
{:ok, [r3_still]} = Ash.read(Reaction |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{}) |> Ash.Query.filter(id == ^reaction3.id), authorize?: false)
result = assert.("reaction3 still archived after restore of comment1", r3_still.archived_at != nil)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
IO.puts("\n--- 12. Purge validation ---")

{:ok, live_post} =

  |> Ash.Changeset.for_create(:create, %{title: "To Purge"})

part.text:
There are issues with the cascade approach. The problem is that when I call `Ash.Changeset.for_update(:restore, ...)` and then try to change attributes, the changeset is already validated. I need to use `force_change_attribute` or restructure the approach.

More fundamentally, the cascade_archive approach of using `after_action` to manually update descendants is fragile. Let me rethink the approach.

The core problem: when archiving a comment, I need to also archive its reactions. The cleanest approach is to use `after_action` hooks that call `Ash.update` directly (not through changesets) on the descendants. But the issue is that calling `for_update` then `change_attribute` after the changeset is already "locked" doesn't work.

Let me use `force_change_attribute` instead:

input.content:
defmodule Forum.Archive.Changes.CascadeArchive do
  @moduledoc """
  Archives a record and all of its descendants that are not already archived.

  All newly archived records receive the same `archived_at` timestamp and the
  same `archive_batch_id`. Records that were already archived before this call
  are left untouched.

  When the target record is already archived, nothing changes anywhere.
  """

  use Ash.Resource.Change

  @impl true
  def change(changeset, _opts, _context) do
    record = changeset.data

    if record.archived_at != nil do
      # Already archived — no-op.
      changeset
    else
      batch_id = Ash.UUID.generate()
      now = DateTime.utc_now()

      changeset
      |> Ash.Changeset.force_change_attribute(:archived_at, now)
      |> Ash.Changeset.force_change_attribute(:archive_batch_id, batch_id)
      |> Ash.Changeset.after_action(fn _changeset, result ->
        cascade_archive(result, now, batch_id)
      end)
    end
  end

  defp cascade_archive(record, now, batch_id) do
    resource = record.__struct__

    case resource do
      Forum.Content.Post ->
        archive_descendants_of_post(record, now, batch_id)

      Forum.Content.Comment ->
        archive_descendants_of_comment(record, now, batch_id)

      Forum.Content.Reaction ->
        {:ok, record}
    end
  end

  defp archive_descendants_of_post(post, now, batch_id) do
    domain = Ash.Resource.Info.domain(Forum.Content.Post)

    query =
      Forum.Content.Comment
      |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{})
      |> Ash.Query.filter(post_id == ^post.id)

    case Ash.read(query, domain: domain, authorize?: false) do
      {:ok, comments} ->
        Enum.reduce_while(comments, {:ok, post}, fn comment, {:ok, _post} ->
          if comment.archived_at != nil do
            {:cont, {:ok, post}}
          else
            comment
            |> Ash.Changeset.new()
            |> Ash.Changeset.force_change_attribute(:archived_at, now)
            |> Ash.Changeset.force_change_attribute(:archive_batch_id, batch_id)
            |> Ash.Changeset.for_update(:restore, %{})
            |> Ash.update(domain: domain, action: :restore, authorize?: false)
            |> case do
              {:ok, updated_comment} ->
                case archive_descendants_of_comment(updated_comment, now, batch_id) do
                  {:ok, _} -> {:cont, {:ok, post}}
                  {:error, error} -> {:halt, {:error, error}}
                end

              {:error, error} ->
                {:halt, {:error, error}}
            end
          end
        end)

      {:error, error} ->
        {:error, error}
    end
  end

  defp archive_descendants_of_comment(comment, now, batch_id) do
    domain = Ash.Resource.Info.domain(Forum.Content.Comment)

    query =
      Forum.Content.Reaction
      |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{})
      |> Ash.Query.filter(comment_id == ^comment.id)

    case Ash.read(query, domain: domain, authorize?: false) do
      {:ok, reactions} ->
        Enum.reduce_while(reactions, {:ok, comment}, fn reaction, {:ok, _comment} ->
          if reaction.archived_at != nil do
            {:cont, {:ok, comment}}
          else
            reaction
            |> Ash.Changeset.new()
            |> Ash.Changeset.force_change_attribute(:archived_at, now)
            |> Ash.Changeset.force_change_attribute(:archive_batch_id, batch_id)
            |> Ash.Changeset.for_update(:restore, %{})
            |> Ash.update(domain: domain, action: :restore, authorize?: false)
            |> case do
              {:ok, _} -> {:cont, {:ok, comment}}
              {:error, error} -> {:halt, {:error, error}}
            end
          end
        end)

      {:error, error} ->
        {:error, error}
    end
  end
end

part.text: Similarly, fix the cascade_restore:

input.content:
defmodule Forum.Archive.Changes.CascadeRestore do
  @moduledoc """
  Restores a record and all of its descendants that share the same `archive_batch_id`.

  On a record that is not archived, nothing changes anywhere.
  On an archived record: the target's `archived_at` and `archive_batch_id` both become `nil`,
  and every descendant whose `archive_batch_id` equals the target's `archive_batch_id`
  (as it was immediately before the call) is restored the same way, recursively.

  Descendants carrying a different `archive_batch_id` are left exactly as they were.
  `:restore` never affects ancestors of the target.
  """

  use Ash.Resource.Change

  @impl true
  def change(changeset, _opts, _context) do
    record = changeset.data

    if record.archived_at == nil do
      # Not archived — no-op.
      changeset
    else
      batch_id = record.archive_batch_id

      changeset
      |> Ash.Changeset.force_change_attribute(:archived_at, nil)
      |> Ash.Changeset.force_change_attribute(:archive_batch_id, nil)
      |> Ash.Changeset.after_action(fn _changeset, result ->
        cascade_restore(result, batch_id)
      end)
    end
  end

  defp cascade_restore(record, batch_id) do
    resource = record.__struct__

    case resource do
      Forum.Content.Post ->
        restore_descendants_of_post(record, batch_id)

      Forum.Content.Comment ->
        restore_descendants_of_comment(record, batch_id)

      Forum.Content.Reaction ->
        {:ok, record}
    end
  end

  defp restore_descendants_of_post(post, batch_id) do
    domain = Ash.Resource.Info.domain(Forum.Content.Post)

    query =
      Forum.Content.Comment
      |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{})
      |> Ash.Query.filter(post_id == ^post.id and archive_batch_id == ^batch_id)

    case Ash.read(query, domain: domain, authorize?: false) do
      {:ok, comments} ->
        Enum.reduce_while(comments, {:ok, post}, fn comment, {:ok, _post} ->
          comment
          |> Ash.Changeset.new()
          |> Ash.Changeset.force_change_attribute(:archived_at, nil)
          |> Ash.Changeset.force_change_attribute(:archive_batch_id, nil)
          |> Ash.Changeset.for_update(:restore, %{})
          |> Ash.update(domain: domain, action: :restore, authorize?: false)
          |> case do
            {:ok, updated_comment} ->
              case restore_descendants_of_comment(updated_comment, batch_id) do
                {:ok, _} -> {:cont, {:ok, post}}
                {:error, error} -> {:halt, {:error, error}}
              end

            {:error, error} ->
              {:halt, {:error, error}}
          end
        end)

      {:error, error} ->
        {:error, error}
    end
  end

  defp restore_descendants_of_comment(comment, batch_id) do
    domain = Ash.Resource.Info.domain(Forum.Content.Comment)

    query =
      Forum.Content.Reaction
      |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived, %{})
      |> Ash.Query.filter(comment_id == ^comment.id and archive_batch_id == ^batch_id)

    case Ash.read(query, domain: domain, authorize?: false) do
      {:ok, reactions} ->
        Enum.reduce_while(reactions, {:ok, comment}, fn reaction, {:ok, _comment} ->
          reaction
          |> Ash.Changeset.new()
          |> Ash.Changeset.force_change_attribute(:archived_at, nil)
          |> Ash.Changeset.force_change_attribute(:archive_batch_id, nil)
          |> Ash.Changeset.for_update(:restore, %{})
          |> Ash.update(domain: domain, action: :restore, authorize?: false)
          |> case do
            {:ok, _} -> {:cont, {:ok, comment}}
            {:error, error} -> {:halt, {:error, error}}
          end
        end)

      {:error, error} ->
        {:error, error}
    end
  end
end

part.text: So by default, a soft destroy returns `:ok`. I need to pass `return_destroyed?: true` to get the record back. Let me update my verification script to handle this:

IO.puts("\n--- 6. Archive comment1 ---")

{:ok, archived_comment1} =
  comment1
  |> Ash.Changeset.for_destroy(:archive, %{}, return_destroyed?: true)
  |> Ash.destroy(authorize?: false)
